assessment.completionStatus: Successful — all four acceptance criteria (AC1–AC4) verified end-to-end against the live MockSite crawl fixtures with the auto-started dev backend.
assessment.successRate: 100% of acceptance criteria (4/4); at the command level, 1 of ~14 invocations needed the documented ./b4w.sh wrapper instead of ./b4w.ps1 (leading-'/' regex value under Git Bash).
assessment.mostConfusingAspects: Shell-wrapper selection on Windows: three launchers (b4w.ps1 / b4w.sh / b4w.bat) and Git Bash's silent '/'-prefix path conversion mean the documented crawl example with -olp "/product/" fails through the wrapper the environment tells you to use, and the caveat lives only in a bundled reference doc, not in --help. Second: a healthy backend being reported as possibly not running by --help --examples.
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Surface the Git Bash leading-'/' caveat (and the ./b4w.sh route) directly in `crawl --help` and the guard's recovery hint. 2) Make --help --examples honest: distinguish 'backend unreachable' from 'backend advertises no tool specs' (the latter is the normal state, since only optional-plugin cliName specs are served). 3) Fix the `createdAt` field so terminal crawl records keep the task's creation instant. 4) Correct the `--args <json>` placeholder to the raw-LoadOptions reality.

issues.title: Leading-'/' flag values (e.g. -olp "/product/") cannot run through ./b4w.ps1 from Git Bash — the CLI's own crawl example fails on the platform's default shell

sections.body:
From Git Bash in the repo root, run the exact command from `crawl --help` Examples:
./b4w.ps1 crawl "http://localhost:18080/generated/crawl/index.html" -d 2 -ol "a.product" -olp "/product/"
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The command runs (as it does via ./b4w.sh), or the crawl help/warning surfaces the required wrapper/caveat at the point of use.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Exit 1: "Error: argument 'C:/Program Files/Git/product/' (probably typed as '/product/') was rewritten by Git Bash's MSYS path conversion ... Run this command via ./b4w.sh instead (it disables the conversion)." The command succeeds only via ./b4w.sh (10 pages fetched, AC2 verified).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Git Bash/MSYS2 rewrites '/' -leading argv tokens into Windows paths before pwsh starts, and the original value is unrecoverable; b4w.ps1's guard (lines ~97–144) correctly detects and refuses it. The gap is disclosure: `crawl --help` shows the very example `-olp "/product/"` with no platform note, and this caveat is documented only in the bundled skill reference (skills/browser4-cli/references/crawl.md § Git Bash/MSYS2 caveat), which a user consulting `--help` never sees. The CLI itself cannot fix the conversion — only surface it.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1:97-144 (MSYS mangled-argument guard); cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:3862 (crawl OptionDefs incl. --out-link-pattern) and the crawl built-in examples block
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a one-line platform note next to --out-link-pattern in `crawl --help` and the `--help --examples` output: "Git Bash: values starting with '/' are path-converted — use ./b4w.sh, MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*', or omit the leading slash (e.g. -olp "product/")".
- Have the b4w.ps1 guard echo the exact de-converted command to run (e.g. MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' ./b4w.ps1 <original argv>) to shorten the recovery loop.
- Mention ./b4w.sh as the Git Bash entry point in the top-level `help` output (the environment's own instructions needed the CLAUDE.md to learn this).
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `--help --examples` always prints "is the backend running?" on a healthy backend (that endpoint is normally empty)

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 status                          # Server health: UP
./b4w.ps1 crawl --help --examples
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8283/mcp/tools/specs   # -> { "tools" : [ ] } in ~3 ms
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either the tool-level examples are printed, or the note states the real reason (this backend advertises no tool-level examples).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: "Tool-level examples are unavailable: is the backend running?" while the same CLI at the same moment is successfully running crawls against that backend.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: build_tool_examples() maps an *empty* spec list to Err("is the backend running?") (main.rs:21333-21335), but GET /mcp/tools/specs only returns specs whose cliName is set (MCPToolController.kt:639, filter `!it.cliName.isNullOrBlank()`); in this checkout only the optional browser4-profile-import plugin declares cliName, so the list is always empty on a stock install — the message is therefore permanently wrong. Compounding it, fetch_tool_spec_values_within() (main.rs:20996) collapses unreachable/timeout/HTTP-error/malformed-body into the same empty Vec, so the CLI cannot tell 'down' from 'no specs'.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:21327 build_tool_examples() / 20996 fetch_tool_spec_values_within(); browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/mcp/controller/MCPToolController.kt:639 listCliToolSpecs()
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Distinguish 'fetch failed' from 'backend answered but advertises no specs': return a reason from the fetch and print "the backend advertises no tool-level examples" for the empty case.
- Make the endpoint (or another one) serve specs for built-in tools too, so --help --examples can deliver what its name promises for e.g. crawl/click.
- Keep the error-flavored wording only for genuine connection failures; when built-in examples printed fine, demote the note to informational.

issues.title: `-a, --args` documented as `<json>` but parsed as a raw LoadOptions string

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 crawl --help   # option line: '-a, --args <json>  Additional LoadOptions passthrough...'  — while the Notes block on the same page says: 'passes additional LoadOptions through as a raw string (e.g. -a "-nMaxRetry 5")'; references/crawl.md shows -a "-requireSize 100000 -scrollCount 5"
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The type placeholder matches what the value actually is.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The value is split on whitespace and forwarded verbatim as LoadOptions tokens (resolve_crawl_args_fallible, main.rs:16645-16666; commands.rs:3958 'Append raw args passthrough'). A user trusting `<json>` would send JSON text and get it forwarded as raw options; the docs contradict themselves within one help page.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Stale OptionDef label: commands.rs:3862 declares `name: "args <json>"` although the passthrough implementation and every example use a raw whitespace-separated options string.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:3862
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Rename the placeholder to `--args <opts>` (or `<load-options>`) and state the raw form with an example in the option description itself.
- If JSON was the intended contract, implement/validate it; otherwise reject JSON-looking values with a hint so the mistake is loud, not silent.

issues.title: crawl status records: `createdAt` silently becomes the finish time on terminal tasks (and is epoch-millis while sibling fields are ISO-8601)

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 crawl "http://localhost:18080/generated/crawl/index.html" -d 3 --refresh -ol "a.product" --background
./b4w.ps1 crawl status <id>    # while Processing:  createdAt=1791900944936 == startedTime 14:15:44.936
./b4w.ps1 crawl cancel <id>
./b4w.ps1 crawl status <id>    # terminal:         createdAt=1791900988787 == finishTime 14:16:28.782 (43 s later)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: `createdAt` is the stable task-creation instant — the code's own comment says it is task identity/age and drives the TTL purge (CrawlSupport.kt:1040-1042).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The running record's createdAt equals the start instant, but every terminal record overwrites it with the completion instant (verified on completed and cancelled tasks; exact millisecond match with finishTime). It is also emitted as raw epoch millis, unlike startedTime/finishTime/fetchedAt which are ISO-8601 strings.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The terminal CrawlResponse builders in CrawlService.kt (completed ~1381, timedOut ~1531, failed ~1589, cancelled ~1688) set startedTime/finishTime but omit `createdAt`, so the data-class default `createdAt: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()` (CrawlModels.kt:133) evaluates at finalization. Only mergeIncrementalProgress carries it forward, so the value visibly changes meaning at completion.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/api/service/crawl/CrawlService.kt (terminal CrawlResponse builders) and CrawlModels.kt:133
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Pass `createdAt = previous?.createdAt ?: <task registration instant>` explicitly in every terminal builder, or capture it once when the task is registered and thread it through.
- Emit it as ISO-8601 like the sibling timestamp fields for consistency in the machine-readable record.
- Add a regression test asserting createdAt is identical while Processing and after completion.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
